why: the EXPLICIT-CODE construction channel a `-fno-exceptions` target needs in place of upstream's throwing constructor (RFC-0089 §"Construction"; phase-427 W2). `Node n; n.init("talker")` and `Node n("talker")` reach the same place; the difference is only whether the failure arrives as a `Result` you must read or as an `ok()` you must ask. rclcpp needs no equivalent because it can throw. Both spellings ship because the arena needs a node in caller-owned storage, so the two-phase form cannot be the odd one out.
